batches.analysis: GenAiAttributesExtractor now emits the exception class as error.type. Add exact OpenAIIoException expectations to chat, streaming-chat, and embedding failure spans and operation-duration metric points in the shared library/javaagent fixtures. Keep successful-operation, exception-event, log, and exact attribute assertions intact.
batches.downsides: Tests intentionally couple the expected error classification to the OpenAI SDK exception type; SDK error-class changes will require an explicit expectation update.
batches.summary: Assert GenAI error types in shared OpenAI failure tests
batches.upsides: Covers the intended fallback on spans and duration metrics across synchronous/asynchronous clients, both exception-signal modes, and baseline/latest SDK test configurations without weakening checks or changing production behavior.

batches.analysis: Record HttpCommonAttributesGetter.getErrorType changing from a default method to a required abstract method in the checked-in current-versus-latest API report. The four added lines exactly match the frozen build's generated drift diff; keep the existing compatibility and report-drift checks intact.
batches.downsides: This records, rather than removes, the intentional source incompatibility; custom HTTP getter implementations still need the newly required method as already documented in the PR changelog.
batches.summary: Refresh the required HTTP getter API compatibility report
batches.upsides: Makes the API report accurately document the PR's declared breaking change and addresses the deterministic build-report drift failure.

diagnoses.analysis: The required-status job explicitly exits 1 when common or latest-dependency jobs fail; its frozen dependencies fail on the OpenAI error assertions and stale API report. Repair those causes, not the aggregation gate.

This job also has unrelated Redis pool-readiness and Couchbase bucket-unavailable failures. The Redis error arises from null redisServerConnections during pool connection initialization; the only PR edit there returns null from getErrorType, exactly matching the former default, and the extraction/callback code is unchanged. Couchbase 3.0 and its tests are unchanged by this PR; both failures are 30-second BUCKET_NOT_AVAILABLE timeouts rather than telemetry assertions. Do not weaken those tests or request a rerun of a run that also contains deterministic PR failures.
